Evan — quick operational suggestion from procurement side (cc Laura who owns vendor agreements):

Proposed language we recommend including in the subprocessor notification/objection section: 

"Provider will notify Customer at least 30 days prior to adding a new subprocessor that will process Customer Personal Data. Customer shall have 10 business days from receipt of notice to object in writing on reasonable grounds. If Customer objects, Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to address Customer's concerns, which may include offering alternative controls or discontinuing use of the proposed subprocessor. In the event the parties cannot agree on a mitigation, either party may terminate the affected Services for the impacted dataset on 60 days' notice."

Rationale: short objection window keeps ops moving but gives procurement time to raise material concerns; termination right is a backstop for critical data classifications. If CliffRise needs a longer review (e.g., 30 business days) we can discuss but it may require a carve-out in the DPA.

Let me know if that aligns — if so, we can put this directly into the DocuSign redline so the clause is explicit.

-Karthik
